Thanks Sofia — appreciate the clear asks. Quick matrix below (high-level):

- Hosted (on-demand / card):
  - Payment: card / self-serve invoicing (small POC)
  - Lead time: immediate
  - Recommended when: validating prompts, small POC (< $5k/mo)
  - Notes: no commit discount; good for 1-3 month evals

- Hosted (committed / reserved via contract):
  - Payment: PO or invoiced (net-30 / net-45 with contract), card sometimes for first invoice
  - Lead time: 1-2 weeks for contract signature + billing setup
  - Recommended when: predictable sustained usage; smaller ops footprint than Dedicated
  - Commit examples: 50M tokens/month (example) -> tiered discounts (5-20% depending on term/volume); common commit windows: 6/12/24 months
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools):
  - Payment: PO / invoice (monthly or annual prepay options)
  - Lead time: 2-6 weeks (capacity and contract)
  - Recommended when: high throughput / strict isolation / dedicated SLAs
  - Commit examples: reserved nodes (e.g., 4x A10G equiv) with minimum 12-month term; discount scales with longer commits and larger node counts
- Private (VPC / on-prem):
  - Payment: enterprise contract + platform fee (PO / invoice)
  - Lead time: 6-12+ weeks (networking, KMS, security reviews)
  - Recommended when: regulated workloads requiring on-prem or VPC isolation
Notes on marketplace: Redwood is in the process of enabling marketplace listings (Azure first). We have an Azure marketplace integration pilot and can offer marketplace quoting for customers who need it — timeline depends on legal/offer setup (can be 2-4 weeks if needed now).

Next steps I propose:
- I'll share a short illustrative pricing appendix (commit tiers + example numbers) and a draft SOW.
- Rishi (cc'd) can confirm standard payment terms and whether we can support net-45 or require net-30 for this account.
- Please confirm procurement contact and target approval date so we can prioritize marketplace or direct contract routing.

Attaching: SOW-draft-Acme-2026.docx (initial language you can share with procurement).

Cheers,
